title: Login returnTo query parameter passed unvalidated to navigate()
description: After login, LoginPage calls navigate(returnTo,{replace:true}) with the raw returnTo query value. The candidate hinged on how react-router 8.4.0 treats absolute, protocol-relative or javascript: targets. The installed library source shows it rejects external targets, so no off-origin redirect or script execution results.
claimed_root_cause: No destination policy (single leading '/', no '//' or scheme) is applied to returnTo before navigate().

trace.description: returnTo is read from URLSearchParams(location.search), default '/'; an attacker can craft the link
login() succeeds with the victim's own credentials; returnTo is unchanged
navigate(returnTo,{replace:true}) goes through react-router's useNavigateUnstable (BrowserRouter, frontend/src/main.tsx:14), whose external-navigation check throws before any history push

evidence.description: useNavigateUnstable calls validateNavigationTarget(to, createHref(path), currentUrl, 'reject') before navigator.push/replace at line 295
With policy 'reject', throws Error('External navigation is not allowed') if the original or resolved URL is not same-origin; covers https://x, //x and javascript:
Installed react-router is v8.4.0 (header comment); frontend/package.json:21 pins 8.4.0
The thrown error lands in the catch block and shows a generic error; the user stays on the SPA origin

reason: Source reading of the installed react-router 8.4.0 settles the blocker (re-checked by the parent). navigate() rejects any external target with a thrown error, so the claimed off-origin redirect or script execution does not occur. Residual effect is a same-origin in-app path or a cosmetic error after a successful login. A '/'-prefix check on returnTo would be harmless defence in depth but is not a vulnerability.
